extracted.intended_audience: early-modern natural philosophers / experimental chemists (readers of a philosophical-chemical treatise)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and experimental considerations for determining whether a constituent (e.g., water, earth, sulphur, mercury) is a true element or merely a produced/derived part of a mixt body; covers sensory, experimental, and methodological standards for analysis. Emphasizes how different agents and operations (fire, distillation, solvents, menstruums) affect outcomes and how to interpret results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chief qualities defining 'water'
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief Qualities which make men give that name to any visible Substance, are, that it is Fluid or Liquid, and that it is insipid and inodorous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text then warns these sensory/physical criteria are insufficient: the so-called phlegme obtained by chymists is rarely perfectly devoid of taste or smell; fluidity can arise from comminution/motion of corpuscles rather than presence of an elemental water; experiments (melting and distilling sea-salt, mixing with spirit of urine) show liquors can be produced from dry bodies without invoking pre-existent water.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensory qualities (taste/smell) are unreliable identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Sapour being an Accident or an Affection of matter that relates to our Tongue, Palate, and other Organs of Tast ... it may very possibly be, that the small Parts of a Body may be of such a Size and Shape ... to be unable to pierce into and make a perceptible Impression upon the Nerves
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not identify a substance as elemental merely because it is insipid or tasteless. Examples: fine threads of silk appear less coloured singly; olive oil can be almost tasteless yet is unlike water. Helmont's insipid liquor should be examined chemically rather than called 'water' on account of insipidity alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fluidity need not indicate presence of elemental water
rubrics_metrics.description: To a Bodies being Fluid there is nothing necessary, but that it be divided into parts small enough; and that these parts be put into such a motion among themselves as to glide some this way and some that way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fluid behavior can be produced by comminution (fire or other agents) producing small corpuscles that act as a liquid; thus liquors obtained by distillation may be result of particle size/shape change rather than liberation of pre-existent water.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fire-products do not prove elemental primacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Those portions ... which the Fire would have presented Us in the forme of Sulphureous and Mercurial Bodies would have, by Helmont's method, been exhibited to us in the form of Salt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observing sulphur or mercury after firing is insufficient to assert they were pre-existing principles; different methods (Helmont's, fire) yield different products — so what appears as a 'principle' may be a product of the agent employed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixedness and tastelessness after fire are insufficient evidence of 'earth'
rubrics_metrics.description: Since a Body from which the Fire hath driven away its looser parts is wont to be look'd upon as Earth, upon the Account of its being endow'd with both these qualities, Tastlessenesse and Fixtnesse ... if it be in the power of Natural Agents to deprive the Caput Mortuum of a body of either of those two Qualities ... the Chymists will not easily define what part of a resolv'd Concrete is earth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Residues (caput mortuum) should not be hastily classified as elemental earth: experiments (Agricola's on Terra Damnata of brimstone; reduction of verdegrease caput mortuum to copper) show residues can yield metals or other substances under further operations. Thus classification must await further examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method-dependence of decomposition (agent matters)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a great Disparity betwixt the Operations of the several Agents whereby the Parts of a Body come to be Dissipated ... the same spirit of Wine will dissociare the Parts of Camphire ... Aqua Fortis will also disjoyn them, and put them into motion; but so as to keep them together, and yet alter their Texture into the form of an Oyle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating constituent nature, consider which agent was used to decompose the body: solvents, fire, or other processes produce different corpuscle sizes and textures and thus different products. Do not generalize from one method to universal elementhood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microstructure (size/figure/texture/motion of corpuscles) determines qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: The varying of either the figure, or the Size, or the Motion, or the Situation, or Connexion, of the Corpuscles whereof any of these Bodies is compos'd, may alter the Fabrick of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Properties often attributed to substantive differences may instead be due to corpuscular arrangement; therefore, explanations of elemental composition should account for particle geometry and motion, not only presumed material essence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Element must be shown to be simple, indestructible, and pre-existent (and this is contested)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Earth be a primary, simple, and indestructible Body ... but till we can be allow'd to examine this Liquor, I think it not unreasonable to doubt whether it be not something else then meer Water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The classical criterion (an element must be simple and indestructible) is questioned: author argues we should not assume pre-existence or permanence without exhaustive demonstration and analysis; alleged elements produced by operations (Helmont's liquors) may be complex.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility and empirical examination required
rubrics_metrics.description: Though his Affirmations conclude strongly ... Yet till we can be allow'd to examine this Liquor, I think it not unreasonable to doubt whether it be not something else then meer Water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims of transmutation (Helmont, Paracelsus) must be verified by examination and reproducible experiments before accepting them as evidence of elemental conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on common chymists' quick pronouncements ('useful' vs 'faeces')
rubrics_metrics.description: I have taken notice of the unwarrantable forwardness of common Chymists to pronounce things useless Fæces, by observing how often they reject the Caput Mortuum of Verdegrease; which is yet so farr from deserving that Name, that not only by strong fires and convenient Additaments it may in some hours be reduc'd into copper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural standard: retain and further investigate residues rather than disposing of them as useless; additional operations may reveal valuable substances (copper, gold).

rubrics_metrics.name: One source can yield many distinct products — undermines fixed-element inference
rubrics_metrics.description: Into all these various Schemes of matter ... may the Water that is imbib'd by the roots of the Vine be brought ... without the visible concurrence of any extraneous Ingredient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because a single starting material (e.g., water taken up by plants) can be transformed into many distinct substances (wood, bark, fruit, spirits, salts), observing diverse products from a material is not decisive proof of pre-existing elemental components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powerful menstruums/agents can alter apparently 'elemental' bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: I know a certain Menstruum ... of so piercing and powerfull a Quality, That ... I have with it really destroy'd even refin'd Gold, and brought it into a Metalline Body of another colour and Nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elemental status should be tested against as wide a range of agents as possible: resistance to common operations does not guarantee an ultimate, indestructible element; the discovery of stronger reagents undermines claims of elementhood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between 'true' elemental identification and artefacts of procedure (e.g., phlegme vs water)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is very possible that dry Bodies may by the Fire be reduc'd to Liquors without any separation of Elements, but barely by a certain kind of Dissipation and Comminution of the matter ... And if it be still objected, that the Phlegme of mixt Bodies must be reputed water, because so weak a tast needs but a very small proportion of Salt to impart it; It may be reply'd ... common Salt ... will yield ... a Liquor, wherein ... Saline Corpuscles abound, Yet there is besides a large proportion of Phlegme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between liquors that are true elemental water and liquors that are aggregates of fine saline corpuscles plus phlegme produced by procedure. Use coagulation, separation (e.g., with mercury) and other tests to determine composition rather than naming by gross appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analogical reasoning and mechanical examples to judge particle effects
rubrics_metrics.description: As Hatchets and Wedges divide it into grosser parts ... Files and Saws makes a Comminution of it into Dust ... the shavings made by the plane being in some things differing ... from those shives or thin and flexible pieces ... obtainable by Borers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating experimental outcomes, consider analogies from mechanical comminution: different 'tools' (agents) produce different particle shapes/sizes and thus different observable products — take method effect into account in interpretation.
